# The subgroup generated by a maximal split torus and rank-one line pairs

This internal support module, in namespace `Langlands.GroupScheme.MaximalSplitSubgroup`, is
part of the proof of `MaximalSplitSubgroupStatement` (Borel–Tits 1965, Théorème 7.2). Over a
field `k`, it constructs the subgroup `F` of a connected reductive group `G` generated by a
maximal split torus `i : S ⟶ G` and line pairs at a family of nonmultipliable roots. It also
lifts the torus, the lines and the Weyl points into `F`.

Notation as in `MaximalSplitSubgroupLines`. `IsGeneratedByFamily A a j` is the Library's
predicate that the closed subgroup `j` is the subgroup generated by the ranges of the
homomorphisms `a o : A o ⟶ G` (module `GeneratedFamily`).

## Declarations

- `lineFamilySource S Idx`: the family of group schemes indexed by `Option (Bool × Idx)`. It
  is `S` at `none` and `Ga k` at every `some (b, d)`.
- `lineFamily i x y`: the family of homomorphisms on these sources. It is `i` at `none`,
  `x d` at `some (true, d)` and `y d` at `some (false, d)`.
- `lineFamilySource_smooth_affine_connected`: for split `S`, every source is smooth, affine
  and connected over `Spec k`.
- `isTorusEquivariant_of_comp`, `relationOver_of_comp`, `commute_of_comp`: let
  `j : F ⟶ G` be a homomorphism whose underlying morphism `j.hom.hom` over `Spec k` is a
  monomorphism. Then torus
  equivariance of a line (`IsTorusEquivariant (f ≫ j) (x ≫ j) α`), the rank-one relation
  `RelationOver (f ≫ j) ν (x ≫ j) (y ≫ j) Z`, and commutation of the images of two points of
  `F` each imply the same statement in `F`, for `f`, `x`, `y` and the points themselves.
- `exists_generated_lineSubgroup`: let `G` be connected reductive, `i` a maximal split torus,
  and `a : Idx → X(S)` a family of roots of `i` with `2 • a d` not a root. Assume that for
  `d ≠ e` and integers `n, m > 0` the character `n • a d - m • a e` is neither zero nor a root.
  Then there are a group scheme `F` over `Spec k`, homomorphisms `j : F ⟶ G` and
  `f : S ⟶ F`, lines `x d, y d : Ga k ⟶ F`, cocharacters `ν d` with `⟨a d, ν d⟩ = 2`, and
  rational points `n d` of `F`, such that:
  - `F` is smooth, affine and connected over `Spec k`;
  - `j` is a closed subgroup (`IsClosedSubgroup j`) and `f ≫ j = i`;
  - `F` is generated, as a subgroup of itself (`IsGeneratedByFamily … (𝟙 F)`), by `f` and
    all the lines `x d`, `y d`;
  - `x d` has weight `a d`, `y d` has weight `-a d`, and `(x d).hom.hom` is a monomorphism;
  - `RelationOver f (ν d) (x d) (y d) Z` holds for every test scheme `Z`;
  - `n d` normalizes `f` through `latticeReflectionIso (a d) (ν d)`;
  - for `d ≠ e`, every point of `x d` commutes with every point of `y e` (over every test
    scheme);
  - for every `d` and every root `c` of `i`, the character `c - ⟨c, ν d⟩ • a d` is a root of
    `i`.

## Proofs

- The three reflection lemmas cancel the monomorphism `j` on the right after pushing it
  through products and inverses (`MonObj.mul_comp`, `GrpObj.inv_comp`).
- `exists_generated_lineSubgroup`. `exists_linePair` (from `MaximalSplitSubgroupLines`)
  gives, for every `d`, lines `xG d`, `yG d` of `G`, a cocharacter `ν d` and a rational
  point `nG d` with all the rank-one properties. The published
  `FiniteGeneration.exists_smooth_generated_family` gives a smooth, affine and connected closed
  subgroup `j : F ⟶ G` generated by `lineFamily i xG yG`. Each member of the family factors
  through `j` (`SubgroupFunctor.IsRepresentedBy.factorHom`). This gives `f`, `x d` and `y d`
  with `f ≫ j = i`, `x d ≫ j = xG d` and `y d ≫ j = yG d`. Put
  `n d = y d(-1) · x d(1) · y d(-1)`. Then `n d ≫ j = nG d`. Generation of `F` by the lifted
  family is `IsGeneratedByFamily.self` (from `MaximalSplitGeneratedMultiplicity`). The
  equivariance, monomorphism, relation and commutation properties follow from those in `G`
  by the reflection lemmas. The commutation in `G` is `commute_of_root_groups`, using the
  root-subgroup ranges of `xG d` and `yG e`. The normalizing property follows from
  `IsNormalizingPoint.of_comp`. The last clause is `sub_pairing_smul_mem_roots`.

## Provenance

This is internal glue for the project's proof of Borel–Tits Théorème 7.2. The subgroup
generated by `S` and the groups `E_{±a}` at the simple nonmultipliable roots is the group
denoted `F` in Borel–Tits 1965, Théorème 7.2 (printed p. 117, PDF p. 64), and in
Conrad–Gabber–Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive groups*, 2nd ed. (2015), proof of Theorem C.2.30,
printed pp. 631–632 (PDF pp. 657–658). Nothing here uses Borel–Tits 3.22.
